trajectory_summary: The call moves from a low-urgency, planning-stage customer to a tentative next-day appointment, driven mainly by the rep's clean handling of the roof/solar bundle question and persistent (if ultimately unsuccessful) attempts to lock down the bill. The appointment is fragile — no bill was actually sent by the end of the call and the rep explicitly conditions the slot on it arriving.
outcome_dispute: This should be read as tentative, not booked. The rep states 'Once you get me that, though, I'll put you in for 09:30 tomorrow' (04:11) — the appointment is explicitly conditional on the bill being sent, which never happens on the call. A time was discussed but not irrevocably locked.

observed_outcome.quote: Once you get me that, though, I'll put you in for 09:30 tomorrow, spot you out for an hour, and they'll give you a roof estimate as well as a solar estimate.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (09:30) were discussed, but the rep explicitly conditions actually booking the slot on receiving the utility bill first, which was not sent during the call — this is agreement in principle without a locked booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No specific bill amount or usage figure was ever stated on this call — the customer only discusses the logistics of sending the bill (already promised to Meg, to be sent via login/download), never a dollar figure or kWh number.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: well, I'm I got a HELOC coming through. I'm planning on using that to I I need to redo my roof.
interest_reason_audit.use_quote: What we could do for you, though, is obviously a solar estimate as well as a roof estimate. So we could do both at the same time.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar' (this is a recycled lead where that groundwork was presumably done with Meg), but the customer volunteered his real motivator/blocker unprompted, and the rep used it immediately to pitch the bundled roof+solar estimate.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: conditional booking left without button-up mechanics
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Once you get me that, though, I'll put you in for 09:30 tomorrow, spot you out for an hour, and they'll give you a roof estimate as well as a solar estimate.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment hinges entirely on a bill that was never sent during the call, and the rep never ran the full button-up sequence (recap, no-driving/computer instruction, 'is that fair?' handshake, text-confirmation promise) to give the customer something concrete to hold onto — this is the highest-risk gap on a call that otherwise built real momentum.

key_moments.stewart_read: On a recycled lead, the rep proactively supplies the prior rep's name when the customer can't recall it, smoothing an awkward moment and signaling continuity/legitimacy of the follow-up.

key_moments.quote: I don't even know if ION has those, but that's another option I wanted to look at.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer asks directly about ground-mount panels. Rep responds immediately and honestly at 02:05 ('we don't do ground mounts') without fumbling, then redirects to what Ion does offer — a clean example of admit-and-recover knowledge-gap handling.

key_moments.quote: Say that again. So when you say roll solar and roof, do you mean, like, roof shingles or panels on the roof?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep answers the customer's direct clarifying question accurately (02:41) but treats it as a definitional Q&A rather than tying the bundle back to the customer's stated HELOC/roof-timing constraint as the reason to act now.

key_moments.quote: Oh, okay. You just haven't gotten that over to us yet?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior unresolved commitment (bill promised to Meg, not yet sent) and cites being busy. Rep confirms the gap but doesn't probe further into why or what would make it easier this time.
